Title: Diagnosis

Details: 
The failing test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet()` tests that a ZipArchiveEntry with more than one Unix permission flag set does not mistakenly return true for `isUnixSymlink()`.

1. `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()` checks whether the Unix mode of the entry indicates it is a symlink by verifying if the Unix mode flags include the symlink flag: `(getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG`.
2. `UnixStat.LINK_FLAG` represents the symbolic link mode bit and equals `0120000` in octal.
3. The `getUnixMode()` method returns the Unix permission bits extracted from the external attributes of the zip entry if the platform is Unix, otherwise zero.
4. The external attributes are stored in a long `externalAttributes` field.
5. The bitmask check in `isUnixSymlink()` only ensures the symlink bit is set but does not exclude the possibility that other bits are also set.
6. The current test entry "META-INF/maven/" likely has multiple mode bits set (e.g., sticky bit, group write bit, etc.), contributing to the Unix permission value `177777` (octal), which includes the symlink bit but also other flags.
7. Because the check is only for the presence of the symlink bit, not that it’s the only bit set, the method incorrectly identifies entries with multiple permission flags including the symlink bit as symlinks.
8. This manifests as `isUnixSymlink()` returning `true` when it should return `false` if more than one flag is set, as the test expects.

The root cause is that `isUnixSymlink()` only checks for the symlink bit presence instead of verifying that the mode has exclusively the symlink bit set. The expected behavior is for `isUnixSymlink()` to return true only if the mode exactly matches the symlink flag alone, or at least does not include any conflicting flags.

No relevant insights were gained from the recent bug reports as they concern other unrelated functionalities.

This explains why the test fails: the mode `177777` (octal) has multiple bits set including the symlink bit, causing the current method logic to misidentify it as a symlink.

The fix should adjust `isUnixSymlink()` to not only check that the symlink bit is set but also that no other bits are set, or at least disallow multiple flag bits for symlink identification.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
